column5: I look over at Valessa and Fortaime. She's fine, and he's shaking.{w}\nHe glances back at me, and I nod, letting him know that things will be fine.{w}\nIt isn't much longer until the suit of armor reaches our location.
column6: 我看向瓦莱莎和福泰姆。她没事，他却在发抖。{w}\n他回头瞥了我一眼，我点点头，让他知道一切都会好起来。{w}\n没过多久，那副铠甲就来到了我们所在的位置。

column5: It stands between all of us, as we press ourselves against the wall.{w}\nIt's almost like it can't see. It has no idea that we're here. That's odd.{w}\nIt even turns its head to the sides, looking straight at us without reacting.
column6: 我们全都紧贴着墙壁，它就站在我们中间。{w}\n它似乎看不见东西，完全不知道我们在这里。真奇怪。{w}\n它甚至把头转向两侧，直勾勾地看着我们却毫无反应。

column5: After a minute or two of standing guard, it turns around and walks away.{w}\nIts steps echo through the tunnels. Loud, metallic, and hollow. It's frightening.{w}\nBut when it's far enough away, we all sigh, and stand at ease. We're safe, now.
column6: 站岗守了一两分钟后，它转过身走开了。{w}\n它的脚步声在隧道中回荡。响亮、金属质感、空洞。真吓人。{w}\n但当它走远后，我们全都松了口气，放松了身体。我们现在安全了。

column5: What was that..?
column6: 那是什么……？

column5: The Triumvirate's Honor Guard.\nThey're the ones that built this underground complex.\nWe find it best not to... interfere with their efforts in any way.
column6: 三人执政团的荣誉卫队。\n这座地下建筑群就是他们建造的。\n我们认为最好……无论如何都别去干涉他们的行动。

column5: Why is that...?
column6: 为什么……？

column5: They're almost like caretakers, so we let them be.\nAll we know for sure, is that they're disobeying their masters.
column6: 他们几乎就像是管理员一样，所以我们由着他们去。\n我们唯一能确定的是，他们正在违抗自己的主人。

column5: Really?
column6: 真的吗？

column5: Yeah. At least, that's what it seems like.\nRather than search for the idol, they built a utopia.\nI think that was the choice of the spirits inside them.
column6: 是啊。至少看起来是这样。\n他们没有去寻找灵像，而是建造了一个乌托邦。\n我觉得那是他们体内那些灵的选择。

column5: Spirits...?
Yeah. They were created by The Blade of Exodus.\nThe spirits inside are victims of their vicious occupation.
column6: 是啊。他们是被流亡之刃创造出来的。\n里面的灵是他们那场残暴占领的受害者。

column5: Right. Then it's just like [firstname] said.\nWait — victims of The Occupation...?
column6: 对。那就跟[firstname]说的一样。\n等等——占领的受害者……？

column5: Right. Then it's just like [firstname] said.\nWait — victims of The Occupation...?
column6: 对。那就跟[firstname]说的一样。\n等等——占领的受害者……？

column5: Yeah. It's sad, really...\nThey want to live again, so they built a home.
column6: 是啊。说来真的很悲哀……\n他们想再次活下去，所以建了一个家。

column5: Valessa looks sad, and takes a few steps back.{w}\nIt doesn't take a genius to realize what she's thinking.{w}\nHaving been a few minutes, our vision has adjusted.
column6: 瓦莱莎神情悲伤，后退了几步。{w}\n不用天才也能看出她在想什么。{w}\n过了几分钟，我们的眼睛已经适应了。

column5: Sorry about that, everybody.\nThose things are brittle, and weak.\nIf we so much as bump them, they fall apart.
column6: 各位，抱歉了。\n那些东西很脆弱，很不结实。\n我们只要稍微碰一下，它们就会散架。

column5: Wait, really...?
column6: 等等，真的吗……？

column5: Yeah. There's nothing inside.\nThey're controlled purely by spiritual energy.\nThey were strong at first, but they're weak now.
column6: 是啊。里面什么都没有。\n它们完全由灵能量驱动。\n一开始它们很强，但现在很弱。

column5: It's almost like it degraded over time.\nWho knows, maybe we can even power them with that blade.\nA bit of irony, right? Using their own forces against them.
column6: 就像是随着时间流逝而退化了一样。\n谁知道呢，也许我们甚至能用那把剑给它们供能。\n有点讽刺，对吧？用他们自己的力量来对付他们。

column5: This is all so complicated...
column6: 这一切也太复杂了……

column5: Yeah, and I'll admit that even I don't know everything.\nBut we won't get to that point if we don't keep moving.
column6: 是啊，我承认，就算是我也不是什么都懂。\n但如果我们不继续前进，就永远到不了那一步。

column5: He motions to the end of the tunnels.
column6: 他朝隧道的尽头示意。

column5: So, shall we...?
column6: 那么，我们走吧……？

column5: We all nod, as we continue to move through the tunnels.{w}\nHowever, Damek seems distracted. There's something on his mind.{w}\nI guess even a man in his position can't have a grasp on everything.
column6: 我们全都点头，继续在隧道中前行。{w}\n不过，达梅克似乎心不在焉。他心里有事。{w}\n我想，即便是他这种地位的人，也不可能事事都了然于胸。

column5: Everyone makes conversation amongst themselves as we continue.{w}\nPerhaps it would be a good idea to talk with Damek a little bit more.{w}\nIt seems like we still have a bit of walking ahead of us after all.
column6: 我们继续前行，大家各自聊着天。{w}\n也许再跟达梅克多聊聊会是个好主意。{w}\n毕竟我们似乎还有一段路要走。

column5: I can see a makeshift doorway at the end of the tunnels.{w}\nThat must be the entrance to the Rebel HQ. Finally.{w}\nIts a bit far away, but I'm glad it's actually in sight.
column6: 我能看到隧道尽头有个临时搭建的门洞。{w}\n那一定是反抗军总部的入口。终于到了。{w}\n虽然还有点远，但总算出现在视野里了，我很高兴。

column5: What's the matter, are your legs sore?
column6: 怎么了，腿酸了吗？

column5: No! Not at all.\nI'm just running out of breath.\nIs it a little stuffy down here, or...?
column6: 没有！完全不是。\n我只是有点喘不过气。\n这下面是不是有点闷，还是……？

column5: Yeah it is.\nDon't worry, you get used to it.\nA small price to pay for privacy, if you ask me.
column6: 确实有点。\n别担心，你会习惯的。\n要我说，为了隐私，这点代价算小的了。

column5: Right...
column6: 好吧……

column5: There are torches lining the tunnels, freshly lit.{w}\nIt must require a lot of maintenance to keep these tunnels accessible.{w} \nI'd hate to be down here when those torches die out. Sounds terrifying.
column6: 隧道两侧排列着火把，刚刚点燃。{w}\n要让这些隧道保持通行，肯定需要大量的维护。{w} \n我可不想在火把熄灭的时候待在这下面。想想就可怕。

column5: Thankfully, they don't seem to be at any risk of fading away.{w}\nWe could stay down here for a while without any worry.{w}\nHowever, that doesn't seem to be on any of our agendas.
column6: 谢天谢地，它们似乎没有熄灭的危险。{w}\n我们大可以放心地在这里待上一阵子。{w}\n不过，这似乎不在我们任何人的计划之中。

column5: There's wooden panels on the floor, almost acting like pavement.{w}\nHowever, it's only a bit more comfortable than the actual floor would be.{w}\nIt's seemingly more for aesthetic purposes than anything regarding comfort.
column6: 地上铺着木板，几乎像是路面一样。{w}\n不过，它也只比真正的地面舒服一点点。{w}\n看起来更多是为了美观，而不是为了舒适。

column5: Drops of humidity and moisture hit the wooden panels, making them split.{w}\nIt looks like they've been here for a while, with clear signs of erosion.{w}\nWith what I know, I'd say that these tunnels are almost twenty years old.
column6: 湿气凝结的水滴落在木板上，让它们开裂。{w}\n看来它们已经在这里很久了，有明显的侵蚀痕迹。{w}\n据我所知，这些隧道大概有将近二十年的历史了。

column5: Hey, Valessa, watch your step!
column6: 嘿，瓦莱莎，小心脚下！

column5: Huh?
column6: 嗯？

column5: There's a bit of a bump here. I almost tripped.
column6: 这里有块凸起。我差点绊倒。

column5: Oh don't worry, I'll be fine.
column6: 哦，别担心，我没事的。

column5: A few moments later, she trips.{w}\nIt was a clear sign that she disregarded his warning.{w}\nHe laughs, and keeps walking forward, highly amused.
column6: 片刻之后，她绊了一下。{w}\n这显然说明她无视了他的警告。{w}\n他大笑起来，兴致勃勃地继续往前走。

column5: Let's not talk about this.
column6: 这事儿就别提了。

column5: As we walk down the tunnels, I make my way to Damek's side.{w}\nI ask him what's on his mind, and the people behind us give us space.{w}\nI'm thankful for their consideration, as we finally get some one-on-one time.
column6: 我们沿着隧道前行，我走到达梅克身边。{w}\n我问他心里在想什么，身后的人给我们留出了空间。{w}\n我很感激他们的体谅，我们终于有了独处的机会。

column5: What's on my mind...?\nOh, it's nothing too major.\nSay — can you keep a secret?
column6: 我心里在想什么……？\n哦，不是什么大事。\n对了——你能保守秘密吗？

column5: Oh, wonderful.\nIts nice to have someone to talk to.
column6: 哦，太好了。\n有个能说说话的人真好。

column5: Again with the flattery...?\nYou already made a good impression, you know.\nIf you keep doing that, I might just get the wrong idea.
column6: 又来这套恭维……？\n你要知道，你已经给我留下好印象了。\n你再这样下去，我可能就要误会了。

column5: Well, it's nothing too bad.\nI just wanted somebody to confide in.
column6: 嗯，不是什么坏事。\n我只是想找个能倾诉的人。

column5: Well, about that...
column6: 嗯，关于那件事……

column5: He blushes and shuffles in place, embarrassed.{w}\nI'm not sure why he trusted me so easily, but I'm not complaining.{w}\nSometimes it's hard for someone in a position of power to have confidants.
column6: 他脸红了，尴尬地原地挪动着脚步。{w}\n我不确定他为什么这么轻易就信任了我，但我并不抱怨。{w}\n有时候，身居高位的人很难有可以倾诉的知己。

column5: About that suit of armor earlier...\nI think I scared everybody with my caution.\nBetween you and I — that was a bit of an exaggeration.
column6: 关于刚才那副铠甲……\n我觉得我的谨慎把大家都吓到了。\n你我之间说句实话——那有点夸张了。

column5: Like I said, those things are brittle, and weak.\nI just didn't want anybody to knock them over, you know?\nIf we kill one of them, what happens to the spirits inside...?
column6: 就像我说的，那些东西很脆弱，很不结实。\n我只是不想让任何人把它们撞倒，你懂吗？\n如果我们毁掉其中一个，里面的灵会怎么样……？

column5: That was a good question, actually.
column6: 其实，那是个好问题。

column5: I want to find a way to {i}free{/i} those spirits trapped inside.\nSomething tells me that killing them won't accomplish that.\nThis is the sole reason why I tell everybody to leave them alone.
column6: 我想找到办法{i}解放{/i}那些被困在里面的灵。\n直觉告诉我，毁掉它们做不到这一点。\n这就是我让大家别去碰它们的唯一原因。

column5: They're harmless. They mind their own business.\nIt's my belief that we should give them the same courtesy.\nThat is, at least, until we find a way to give them all freedom.
column6: 它们没有恶意，只顾自己的事。\n我认为我们也该以同样的礼数对待它们。\n至少，在我们找到让它们全部获得自由的办法之前是这样。

column5: Though they don't serve The Triumvirate, they're still trapped.\nNobody should be forced into a position like that. They're just like us.\nSpirits of family, and friends. Spirits of innocent occupation victims.
column6: 虽然它们不为三人执政团效力，但它们依然被困着。\n没有人该被逼到那种境地。它们和我们一样。\n是家人、朋友的灵。是无辜占领受害者的灵。

column5: He lets out a loud sigh, like the ability to vent is a godsend.{w}\nI can tell that this is something he's been keeping inside for a while.
column6: 他长长地叹了口气，仿佛能宣泄出来是天赐的恩惠。{w}\n我看得出来，这件事他已经憋在心里很久了。

column5: Sorry for rambling on.\nI think I'm just trying to defend myself.\nLast week, I accidentally bumped into one...
column6: 抱歉，我啰嗦了。\n我想我只是在为自己辩解。\n上周，我不小心撞到了一个……

column5: It crumbled, and fell to the ground.\nI felt absolutely awful. It's like I {i}killed{/i} them.\nWho knows how many spirits were inside that {i}one{/i} suit.
column6: 它碎裂开来，倒在了地上。\n我心里难受极了。就像是我{i}杀了{/i}它们一样。\n谁知道那{i}一副{/i}铠甲里有多少灵呢。

column5: I mean, in this war — I have to draw blood. I have to kill.\nBut normally, I reserve that punishment for our enemies.\nWe're talking about the spirits of long lost family here, [firstname].
column6: 我是说，在这场战争里——我不得不见血，不得不杀人。\n但通常，我把那种惩罚留给我们的敌人。\n可这里说的是逝去已久的家人的灵啊，[firstname]。

column5: I mean, in this war — I have to draw blood. I have to kill.\nBut normally, I reserve that punishment for our enemies.\nWe're talking about the spirits of long lost family here, [firstname].
column6: 我是说，在这场战争里——我不得不见血，不得不杀人。\n但通常，我把那种惩罚留给我们的敌人。\n可这里说的是逝去已久的家人的灵啊，[firstname]。

column5: I feel like I did something wrong.\nI almost feel like I'm a murderer, you know?\nIt's odd how blurred those lines can be in war.
column6: 我觉得自己做错了事。\n我几乎觉得自己像个杀人犯，你知道吗？\n在战争中，这些界限竟会如此模糊，真是奇怪。

column5: Kill the enemy leader? You're nothing short of a hero.\nBut kill a citizen going about their business? You're a monster.\nMaybe at the end of the day, that's what we are. Monsters.
column6: 杀了敌方首领？你就是个英雄。\n但杀了一个过着自己日子的平民？你就是个怪物。\n也许说到底，我们就是这样。怪物。

column5: Maybe once this is all over, I'll believe that.\nI guess there's one big difference between us and them.\nWhen {i}we{/i} rule the world, we'll {i}stop{/i} killing. That's not {i}us{/i}.
column6: 也许等这一切结束后，我会相信这一点。\n我想我们和他们之间有一个很大的区别。\n当{i}我们{/i}统治世界时，我们会{i}停止{/i}杀戮。那不是{i}我们{/i}。

column5: I wish that's what I felt like. \nThere's just so much pressure.\nI guess you know what it's like.
column6: 我希望我也能这么觉得。 \n压力实在太大了。\n我想你知道那是什么滋味。

column5: I guess you're right.\nAfter this is over, things will be better.\nWe aren't like The Triumvirate. We don't {i}want{/i} to kill.
column6: 我想你说得对。\n等这一切结束后，情况会好起来的。\n我们不像三人执政团。我们并不{i}想{/i}杀人。

column5: We continue walking down the tunnels, while he vents.{w}\nI can understand where he's coming from, and I can relate.{w}\nIt was all about the greater good, regardless of what we did.
column6: 他倾诉着，我们继续沿着隧道前行。{w}\n我能理解他的想法，也能感同身受。{w}\n无论我们做了什么，一切都是为了大局。

column5: Everybody expects me to lead us to victory.\nThey call me a master strategist, and shower me with praise.\nBut at the end of the day, I'm just following in {i}his{/i} footsteps.
column6: 所有人都指望我带领大家走向胜利。\n他们称我为战略大师，对我赞不绝口。\n但说到底，我只是在追随{i}他{/i}的脚步。

column5: Salus was the master strategist. I just worked under him.\nThey say I fill his shoes quite well, but I don't think that's true.\nI think they need something to believe in. They need hope.
column6: 萨卢斯才是真正的战略大师。我只是在他手下做事。\n他们说我很好地接替了他，但我不这么认为。\n我觉得他们需要一个可以信仰的东西。他们需要希望。

column5: They pushed that need for hope onto me, and I {i}became{/i} that hope.\nHonestly, I think I'm more of a symbol than anything else.\nI'm sure you know what I mean. You're The Seer.
column6: 他们把对希望的渴求强加到我身上，而我{i}成为{/i}了那份希望。\n说实话，我觉得自己更像一个象征，而不是别的什么。\n我敢肯定你明白我的意思。你是先知。

column5: They pushed that need for hope onto me, and I {i}became{/i} that hope.\nHonestly, I think I'm more of a symbol than anything else.\nI'm sure you know what I mean. You're The Seeress.
column6: 他们把对希望的渴求强加到我身上，而我{i}成为{/i}了那份希望。\n说实话，我觉得自己更像一个象征，而不是别的什么。\n我敢肯定你明白我的意思。你是先知。

column5: You had this role thrust upon you whether you wanted it or not.\nIt's kind of the same for me. I'm The General. I had no say in the matter.\nThis pressure, and all those expectations? I'm afraid I might break.
column6: 无论你愿不愿意，这个角色都被强加到了你身上。\n对我来说也差不多。我是将军。这事由不得我做主。\n这份压力，还有那些期望？我怕我会撑不住。

column5: Do you have any advice?
column6: 你有什么建议吗？

column5: Together...? Like a second-in-command?\nI actually like the sound of that. We'd be a team.\nSomething to think about, at least. Thank you.
column6: 一起……？就像副手那样？\n我其实挺喜欢这个说法。我们会成为一支队伍。\n至少，值得考虑。谢谢你。

column5: You don't think that would make them doubt...?\nTheir “mighty” leader, full of stress and worry?\nI only told you because I thought you could relate.
column6: 你不觉得那会让他们心生怀疑吗……？\n他们“伟大”的领袖，却满是压力和忧虑？\n我告诉你只是因为我觉得你能感同身受。

column5: But I guess honesty {i}is{/i} the best solution.\nMaybe I should lower their expectations a bit, yeah?\nI'm just {i}Damek{/i}. I'm not some invincible symbol of hope.
column6: 但我想诚实{i}确实{/i}是最好的办法。\n也许我该稍微降低一下他们的期望，对吧？\n我只是{i}达梅克{/i}。我不是什么无敌的希望象征。

column5: Brutally honest, I see.\nI wish I had that kind of courage.\nMore than anything, I want to please everyone.
column6: 看得出来，你真是直率得毫不留情。\n我希望我也有那样的勇气。\n比起任何事，我都想取悦所有人。

column5: But in a position of power, that's impossible.\nI might have to start making tough calls in the future.\nWell, more tough than I've been doing so far, I mean.
column6: 但身处高位，那是不可能的。\n将来我可能得开始做一些艰难的决定。\n嗯，我是说，比我到目前为止做的还要艰难。

column5: Well, we could all die.\nWe need to have {i}some{/i} sort of plan.\nI can't gamble with the lives of our forces.
column6: 嗯，我们可能会全军覆没。\n我们必须有{i}某种{/i}计划。\n我不能拿我们部队的性命去赌。

column5: A more common struggle than I realize, I guess.\nMaybe I should be honest and open with the rebels.\nWho knows — maybe a bunch of them could relate to me.
column6: 我想，这种挣扎比我意识到的更普遍。\n也许我该对反抗军坦诚相待。\n谁知道呢——也许他们中有不少人能理解我。

column5: After all, we're in this thing together.\nThe fate of the world isn't just on {i}my{/i} shoulders.\nEvery one of our rebels has a massive burden upon them.
column6: 毕竟，我们是一条船上的。\n世界的命运不只压在{i}我{/i}一个人肩上。\n我们每一个反抗军成员都背负着沉重的担子。

column5: I guess there's not much more we can do, huh?\nPerhaps we'll have some more time to talk later on.\nMy doors are always open to you, [firstname]. I promise.
column6: 我想我们也没什么别的能做了，对吧？\n也许以后我们还有时间再聊。\n我的门永远为你敞开，[firstname]。我保证。

column5: I guess there's not much more we can do, huh?\nPerhaps we'll have some more time to talk later on.\nMy doors are always open to you, [firstname]. I promise.
column6: 我想我们也没什么别的能做了，对吧？\n也许以后我们还有时间再聊。\n我的门永远为你敞开，[firstname]。我保证。

column5: He gives me a slight smile, and we continue to walk.{w}\nThe end of the tunnels is growing ever closer.{w}\nIt seemed like this leg of the journey was over.
column6: 他朝我微微一笑，我们继续往前走。{w}\n隧道的尽头越来越近了。{w}\n看来这段旅程就要结束了。

column5: As soon as we exit the tunnels, it's immediately easier to breathe.{w}\nSunlight pierces through the ceiling, with the surface in sight.{w}\nThose tunnels must've started low and worked their way up.
column6: 我们一走出隧道，呼吸就立刻顺畅了许多。{w}\n阳光穿透天花板，地面已映入眼帘。{w}\n那些隧道肯定是从低处开始，一路向上延伸的。

column5: However, the exposure to the surface doesn't compromise our privacy.{w}\nThere's no way anybody would find this place unless they knew about it.{w}\nAnd from what I could tell, only a select few did. So we were perfectly safe.
column6: 不过，与地面的连通并没有损害我们的隐秘性。{w}\n除非事先知道，否则没人能找到这个地方。{w}\n而据我所知，只有极少数人知道。所以我们绝对安全。

column5: Home, sweet home.\nI'd like to welcome you all to our new HQ.\nIt took some “coercing” with The Mayor, but it's ours.
column6: 金窝银窝，不如自己的狗窝。\n欢迎各位来到我们的新总部。\n虽然跟市长“协商”了一番，但这里归我们了。

column5: Wow, this place is incredible!\nAnd The Honor Guard built all of it?
column6: 哇，这地方太不可思议了！\n而且全是荣誉卫队建的？

column5: Essentially, yeah.\nWith a few finishing touches by ourselves.\nThis is what they've been working on for twenty years.
column6: 基本上是的。\n我们自己做了些收尾工作。\n这就是他们二十年来的心血。

column5: That's crazy...\nAll of those weapons, too!\nIt's almost like they made it just for us.
column6: 太疯狂了……\n还有那些武器！\n简直就像是专门为我们打造的一样。

column5: We can dream, but I doubt it.\nHey, Ulric — Pro? Can you show them around?
column6: 可以做做梦，但我不这么认为。\n嘿，乌尔里克——普洛？能带他们四处看看吗？

column5: He motions toward Valessa and Fortaime.
column6: 他朝瓦莱莎和福泰姆示意。

column5: Sure.
column6: 当然。

column5: You got it, boss!
column6: 没问题，老大！

column5: Pro is being overly polite, likely to make it up to Damek.{w}\nHe sneers at Pro in reply, still a little upset at his slight delay.{w}\nHowever, moments later, they all leave the room together.
column6: 普洛过分礼貌，大概是想弥补达梅克。{w}\n达梅克则嗤笑一声作为回应，对他那点耽搁还有些不快。{w}\n不过，片刻之后，他们就一起离开了房间。

column5: Damek turns to face me, with just the two of us in the lobby.{w}\nA few rebels run from room to room, going about their business.{w}\nI can tell from the way that they move that they don't want to disturb us.
column6: 达梅克转过身面对我，大厅里只剩我们两人。{w}\n几个反抗军成员在各个房间之间穿梭，忙着自己的事。{w}\n从他们走动的样子我能看出，他们不想打扰我们。

column5: Well, what do you think?\nThis is it — this is our home.
column6: 那么，你觉得怎么样？\n就是这里了——这就是我们的家。

column5: I know, right?\nI thought the same thing.\nIt's incredible that they made this.
column6: 我也这么想，对吧？\n我当初也是同样的感受。\n他们能造出这个，真是太不可思议了。

column5: What? That's not—\nYou know what I meant, [firstname]!
column6: 什么？那不是——\n你知道我是什么意思，[firstname]！

column5: What? That's not—\nYou know what I meant, [firstname]!
column6: 什么？那不是——\n你知道我是什么意思，[firstname]！

column5: Oh, trust me — we did!\nIt was ten times worse before this.\nI wanted only the best for someone like you.
column6: 哦，相信我——我们尽力了！\n在这之前，这里糟上十倍。\n对你这样的人，我只想给你最好的。

column5: Well, it's already had twenty years.\nWhat's a few more — am I right?\nLet's just call it a fixer-upper.
column6: 嗯，它都已经存在二十年了。\n再多几年又算什么——对吧？\n就当它是个需要修缮的房子吧。

column5: He smiles and shuffles in place.
column6: 他笑了笑，原地挪动着脚步。

column5: Well, time to start the grand tour?\nLet's see, where should we go first...?
column6: 那么，是时候开始盛大参观了？\n让我想想，我们该先去哪儿……？

column5: He places a hand on his chin, losing himself in thought.
column6: 他一只手托着下巴，陷入沉思。

column5: Ah, of course!\nThe Library, and The Barracks.
column6: 啊，当然了！\n图书馆，还有兵营。

column5: He points to two of the nearby doors.
column6: 他指向附近的两扇门。

column5: The Library is great for studying.\nAnd The Barracks? That's for socializing.\nYou'll definitely want to meet your new allies.
column6: 图书馆很适合研习。\n兵营呢？那是用来社交的。\n你肯定想认识认识你的新盟友。

column5: So, let's start with those...\nAfter that, we can go to your personal quarters.\nThat's right — all of you are getting your own rooms.
column6: 那么，我们就从这些开始吧……\n之后，我们可以去你们的私人住处。\n没错——你们每个人都会有自己的房间。

column5: My own room? That was pretty impressive.{w}\nThis place must go deeper than I thought.{w}\nI nod and smile, as I start to follow Damek.
column6: 我自己的房间？这真让人印象深刻。{w}\n这地方一定比我想象的还要深。{w}\n我点点头，微笑着，开始跟着达梅克走。

column5: We were finally here. I felt like I could relax, now.{w}\nThis entire journey has just been one thing after another.{w}\nBut now I can rest, and have privacy? I'll never take it for granted again.
column6: 我们终于到了。我觉得现在可以放松了。{w}\n这一整段旅程就是一件接一件的事。{w}\n但现在我能休息，还能有隐私？我再也不会把这当作理所当然了。

column5: The Library and The Barracks are accessed through this area.{w}\nUse the map icons by the two doors to navigate to these optional areas.{w}\nTo move to your personal quarters, you must return to the region map.
column6: 图书馆和兵营都要经过这个区域才能进入。{w}\n使用两扇门旁的地图图标前往这些可选区域。{w}\n要前往你的私人住处，你必须返回区域地图。

column5: There's light piercing through the ceiling.{w}\nThis slight exposure to the surface makes it much less stuffy.{w}\nIt's easier to breathe here, and everybody seems happy about that.
column6: 有光线穿透天花板照射进来。{w}\n与地面的这点连通让这里没那么闷了。{w}\n在这里呼吸更顺畅，大家似乎都为此感到高兴。

column5: However, the light illuminates the dust lining almost everything.{w}\nWe can even see the dust permeating the air. That's kind of gross.{w}\nWith every breath I take, I'm worried I might breathe some in.
column6: 然而，光线照亮了几乎覆盖在一切表面的灰尘。{w}\n我们甚至能看到空气中弥漫的灰尘。有点恶心。{w}\n每吸一口气，我都担心会吸进一些灰尘。

column5: There's a rack full of swords, almost in pristine condition.{w}\nDamek was right. The Honor Guard really left them everything.{w}\nThis place is a fortress, and their army is much larger than I thought.
column6: 有一个挂满剑的架子，几乎完好如新。{w}\n达梅克说得对。荣誉卫队真的把一切都留给了他们。{w}\n这地方是座堡垒，他们的军队也比我以为的庞大得多。

column5: These doors are blocked by countless crates and supplies.{w}\nI guess there's nothing of purpose behind those doors.{w}\nIt seems that only the library and barracks are important.
column6: 这些门被无数板条箱和补给堵住了。{w}\n我猜那些门后面没有什么要紧的东西。{w}\n看来只有图书馆和兵营比较重要。

column5: However, Damek also mentioned the crew quarters and war table.{w}\nOne of the doors in this massive room must lead deeper inside.{w}\nI almost have a hard time believing those suits of armor made this.
column6: 不过，达梅克还提到了船员宿舍和作战桌。{w}\n这个巨大房间里的某扇门一定通向更深处。{w}\n我几乎难以相信那些铠甲造出了这一切。

column5: Cannot access content at this time.\nIf there is an X, you must complete preceding Heart-to-Hearts.\nIf there is a checkmark, you must move on to the next Heart-to-Heart.
column6: 目前无法访问此内容。\n如果显示 X，你必须先完成前面的心灵交流。\n如果显示对勾，你必须继续下一个心灵交流。

column5: We enter the barracks, and Damek quickly looks around.{w}\nThere's a bunch of rebels, practicing with swords.{w}\nThose training dummies seem to get a lot of use.
column6: 我们走进兵营，达梅克迅速环顾四周。{w}\n有一群反抗军成员在练习剑术。{w}\n那些训练假人看起来使用得很频繁。

column5: Well, this is basically our training room.\nIt's a great place to socialize as well.\nI'd consider it our main hub, actually.
column6: 嗯，这里基本上就是我们的训练室。\n也是个很棒的社交场所。\n其实，我会把它当作我们的主要活动中心。

column5: If you can't find a comrade, they're probably in here.\nThere's a bunch of seats in the back for when we eat meals.\nI guess that makes it a bit of a cafeteria too, doesn't it?
column6: 如果你找不到某个同伴，他们多半就在这里。\n后面有很多座位，供我们吃饭时用。\n我想这也让它有点像食堂了，对吧？

column5: Anyway, there's not much more to say.\nMake use of this room at your leisure.\nI'll meet you back outside when you're ready.
column6: 总之，也没什么更多好说的了。\n随你方便，尽管使用这个房间。\n你准备好了就到外面找我。

column5: He makes his way back to the main hall.{w}\nI stand and watch the rebels practice their swordplay.{w}\nThere's so many of them. This really was a sizable army.
column6: 他返回了大厅。{w}\n我站着观看反抗军成员练习剑术。{w}\n他们人数真多。这确实是一支规模可观的军队。

column5: In this room, you can re-watch all previous Party Banter.{w}\nIt's great to revisit content without moving through a ton of old areas.{w}\nClick the letters for a list of which Party Banter is located in which grid spot.
column6: 在这个房间里，你可以重看之前所有的队伍闲聊。{w}\n不用重走大量旧区域就能重温内容，真是太好了。{w}\n点击字母，查看哪段队伍闲聊位于哪个网格位置。

column5: So, this might be the last time we see the town square.\nIs there anything we should do before we go...?
column6: 所以，这可能是我们最后一次看到城镇广场了。\n走之前我们还有什么该做的吗……？

column5: I guess one last drink would be nice.\nThe water from Valinorth is always so pure.\nWant to share some with me, Valessa?
column6: 我想最后再喝一杯应该不错。\n瓦利诺斯的水总是那么纯净。\n要跟我一起喝点吗，瓦莱莎？

column5: Sure, we can use the cups I left here earlier.\nI was just finishing my water run when we all met up.
column6: 当然可以，我们可以用我之前留在这儿的杯子。\n大家碰头的时候，我刚打完水回来。

column5: So what should we toast to?
column6: 那我们该为什么干杯呢？

column5: Toast...?
column6: 干杯……？

column5: Yeah, this is a big day, right?\nWe should probably drink to {i}something{/i}.\nEspecially if it's the last time we might be here.
column6: 是啊，今天是重要的日子，对吧？\n我们总该为{i}点什么{/i}喝一杯。\n尤其是如果我们可能是最后一次来这里的话。

column5: Oh, let's see...
column6: 哦，让我想想……

column5: What about \"new beginnings\"?\nOr something like \"being with friends\"?
column6: 为“新的开始”怎么样？\n或者类似“与朋友相伴”之类的？

column5: What about \"new beginnings {i}with{/i} friends\"?\nI think that's rather fitting for us.
column6: 为“{i}与{/i}朋友一起的新的开始”怎么样？\n我觉得这对我们挺贴切的。

column5: Sounds good to me.\nTo new beginnings with friends.\nMay our bonds never break.
column6: 我觉得不错。\n为与朋友一起的新的开始。\n愿我们的羁绊永不破裂。

column6:
A1 - 最后一次共饮

A3 - 守门的工作
A4 - 鹿角的麻烦

column5: Wow, it's so beautiful inside The Grand Tree.\nToo bad they rarely let the scribe-in-training come here.\nI wish I had more time to spend in Valinorth.
column6: 哇，巨树里面真美。\n可惜他们很少让见习书记官来这里。\n我真希望能有更多时间待在瓦利诺斯。

column5: Actually, that's not a scribe-in-training rule.\nIt was more like a Fortaime rule, no offense.
column6: 其实，那不是针对见习书记官的规定。\n更像是针对福泰姆的规定，无意冒犯。

column5: What's that supposed to mean!?
column6: 那是什么意思！？

column5: You're not exactly a quiet person.\nThis is a sacred place, and silence is essential.
column6: 你可算不上是个安静的人。\n这里是神圣之地，安静是必须的。

column5: Why didn't you tell me...?\nI would've been quiet, I promise.\nJust like when I go to the library.
column6: 你为什么不告诉我……？\n我会安静的，我保证。\n就像我去图书馆时那样。

column5: Hey, I don't make up the rules.\nBut honestly, I wish I would've fought it.\nI didn't realize our time here would be so limited.
column6: 嘿，规定又不是我定的。\n但说实话，我真希望自己当初抗争过。\n我没意识到我们在这里的时间会这么有限。

column5: I thought we'd be here until we were old and gray.\nBut to think that Valinorth would just be a small phase...?\nYou're not the only one who has regrets, Fortaime.
column6: 我以为我们会在这里待到白发苍苍。\n可谁能想到瓦利诺斯只是一个短暂的阶段……？\n有遗憾的不止你一个，福泰姆。

column5: At least you were allowed inside...!\nI was kept out because of my big mouth?
column6: 至少你还能进去……！\n而我却因为大嘴巴被挡在门外？

column5: Well, I guess I'm the only one to blame...\nI'll try to watch my mouth from now on.
column6: 嗯，我想只能怪我自己……\n从今往后我会尽量管住自己的嘴。

column5: I give you ten minutes, tops.
column6: 我赌你顶多撑十分钟。

column5: Hey!
column6: 嘿！

column5: Hey, Zamira. What's work like?
column6: 嘿，扎米拉。你的工作是什么样的？

column5: It's a lot less exciting than you'd think.\nThey advertise it as a position of power.\nBusting smugglers, and protecting Valinorth.
column6: 远没有你想象的那么刺激。\n他们把它宣传成一个有权势的职位。\n打击走私贩，保护瓦利诺斯。

column5: And it's not like that?
column6: 结果不是那样？

column5: No, not at all!\nI spend most of my day standing around.\nCrime in Valinorth is almost non-existent.
column6: 不，完全不是！\n我一天大部分时间都站着发呆。\n瓦利诺斯几乎没有犯罪。

column5: Because the spirits have blessed us, right?
column6: 因为灵保佑了我们，对吧？

column5: I guess that's one popular theory.\nBut to be honest, I don't buy it.\nSpirits can't change our nature.
column6: 这大概是一种流行的说法。\n但说实话，我不信。\n灵改变不了我们的本性。

column5: Nature...?
column6: 本性……？

column5: Deep down inside, we're all evil.\nSome of us just manage it better than others.\nWe all have our impulses. It's about controlling them.
column6: 在内心深处，我们都是邪恶的。\n只不过有些人比别人更善于控制。\n我们都有冲动。关键在于控制它们。

column5: What an odd outlook.
column6: 这观点真奇怪。

column5: Hey, don't deny your impulses, Valessa.\nIf you had to steal to get by, you'd do it.\nValinorth is just special. Resources are everywhere.
column6: 嘿，别否认你的冲动，瓦莱莎。\n如果为了活下去不得不去偷，你也会做的。\n瓦利诺斯只是很特别。资源到处都是。

column5: Mazeo has been almost completely deforested.\nYou can't just go into the forest and find food.\nThere's not much natural running water, either.
column6: 马泽奥几乎被彻底砍伐殆尽。\n你没法随便走进森林就找到食物。\n天然活水也不多。

column5: See, I didn't know that...
column6: 你看，我之前都不知道……

column5: I don't blame you.\nEveryone in Valinorth is happy.\nNobody is scraping by, you know?
column6: 我不怪你。\n瓦利诺斯人人都很幸福。\n没有人过得紧巴巴的，你知道吗？

column5: Imagine if food was scarce.\nThere'd be a lot more people breaking the law.\nStealing it, hurting others for it, you name it.
column6: 想象一下如果食物短缺。\n会有多得多的人违法。\n偷食物、为了食物伤害别人，什么都有。

column5: How do you know about all of this?
column6: 你怎么会知道这些？

column5: I've been to Mazeo a couple of times.\nTrust me, the guards there have it {i}much{/i} harder.\nThey don't even know if they'll survive their shifts.
column6: 我去过马泽奥几次。\n相信我，那里的守卫日子{i}难{/i}过得多。\n他们连自己能不能活着值完班都不知道。

column5: Oh, wow...
column6: 哦，哇……

column5: So when I say the post here in Valinorth is boring?\nI'm not really complaining, to be totally honest.\nI'd much prefer boring work, to you know — dying.
column6: 所以当我说瓦利诺斯这里的岗位很无聊时？\n说实话，我并不是真的在抱怨。\n比起——你懂的，死掉，我宁愿要无聊的工作。

column5: Hey Zamira, about those antlers.
column6: 嘿，扎米拉，关于那对鹿角。

column5: What about them?
column6: 鹿角怎么了？

column5: You ever like, hit them on a doorway?\nI mean, you can't be fully aware of them all the time.\nOh! Have you ever accidentally hit someone else with them?
column6: 你有没有，比如，用它们撞到过门框？\n我是说，你不可能时时刻刻都完全留意到它们。\n哦！你有没有不小心用它们撞到过别人？

column5: I'm about to...
column6: 我马上就要……

column5: Whoa, okay, backing off...!\nI was just curious. I've always wondered.\nHow do you put a shirt on each morning?
column6: 哇，好吧，我退后……！\n我只是好奇。我一直想知道。\n你每天早上是怎么穿衬衫的？

column5: What do you mean?
column6: 你什么意思？

column5: Well you can't really slip clothes over your head.\nThose things would tear through any fabric.
column6: 你总没法把衣服从头上套下去吧。\n那玩意儿会把任何布料都戳破的。

column5: I don't really have anything that slips over my head.\nI only wear things I can put my arms inside of first.\nYou know, like button ups, or vests?
column6: 我没有什么需要从头上套的衣服。\n我只穿能先把胳膊伸进去的衣服。\n你知道，比如系扣衬衫，或者马甲？

column5: Right. I guess that makes sense.\nSorry for annoying you. Please don't hit me!
column6: 对。我想这说得通。\n抱歉烦到你了。请别打我！

column5: Of course. I'll do my best, Fortaime.\nBut I'm not responsible for any \"accidents\".
column6: 当然。我会尽力的，福泰姆。\n但任何“意外”我可不负责。

column5: What!? No fair! How did you beat me...?
column6: 什么！？不公平！你怎么赢我的……？

column5: Even with a head start, you're no match for me.\nTime to throw in the towel. Stick to climbing trees.
column6: 就算让你先跑，你也不是我的对手。\n认输吧。你还是去爬树吧。

column5: Oh, so you want to have a climbing race?
column6: 哦，所以你想来场爬树比赛？

column5: I'll pass, thanks.
column6: 不用了，谢谢。

column5: Wait, why...?
column6: 等等，为什么……？

column5: A smart person doesn't pick a battle they know they'll lose.\nI'm surprised you challenged me Fortaime, you know how fast I am.
column6: 聪明人不会去打明知会输的仗。\n你居然敢挑战我，福泰姆，你知道我有多快。

column5: Are you calling me stupid!?
column6: 你是在说我蠢吗！？

column5: No, I'd {i}never{/i} do that.
column6: 不，我{i}绝不会{/i}那么做。

column5: Anyway, isn't the spirit idol beautiful?
column6: 总之，那座灵像是不是很美？

column5: That's putting it lightly.\nIt's one of the coolest things I've ever seen.\nWhen it's lit up, it must be incredible.
column6: 这说得太轻描淡写了。\n那是我见过最酷的东西之一。\n当它亮起来的时候，一定美得惊人。

column5: Yeah, I'd pay almost any price to see that.\nBut don't worry Fortaime, I'm sure there's something we can do.\nIf we all work together, we can make that idol shine again.
column6: 是啊，为了看到那个，我几乎愿意付出任何代价。\n但别担心，福泰姆，我相信我们一定有办法。\n如果我们齐心协力，就能让那座灵像重新闪耀。

column5: Wow Ulric, it's so big!
column6: 哇，乌尔里克，它好大！

column5: Yeah, I get compliments on it all the time.
column6: 是啊，我一直都收到关于它的赞美。

column5: C-can I touch it...?
column6: 我、我能摸摸它吗……？

column5: Of course you can.\nJust be gentle, though.
column6: 当然可以。\n不过要温柔点。

column5: Yeah, I'll do my best.
column6: 好，我会尽量的。

column5: Whoa — it's heavier than I thought!
column6: 哇——比我想的要重！

column5: You might want to use both hands.\nAnd tighten your grip a little bit.
column6: 你最好用两只手。\n再握紧一点。

column5: Like this...?
column6: 这样……？

column5: A little bit lower.
column6: 再低一点。

column5: Oh, sure.\nHow about now?
column6: 哦，好。\n现在呢？

column5: There you go. That's more like it.\nNow swing that sword with all your might!
column6: 这就对了。这样好多了。\n现在用尽全力挥剑！

column5: Hyaa—!
column6: 哈呀——！

column5: Whoa — watch what you're doing!\nYou could've killed me, kid.
column6: 哇——小心点！\n你差点杀了我，小子。

column5: I'm so sorry! \nI've never used a greatsword before.
column6: 非常抱歉！ \n我以前从没用过巨剑。

column5: I feel like we should keep it that way.
column6: 我觉得还是保持这样比较好。

column5: Oh, hey Zamira!\nIt's good to see you again.\nI was starting to worry you might...
column6: 哦，嘿，扎米拉！\n很高兴又见到你。\n我都开始担心你可能会……

column5: Oh, come on now.\nThere's no need to worry about me.\nI'd worry about Valinorth. There's no more gate guard.
column6: 哦，得了吧。\n没必要担心我。\n你该担心瓦利诺斯。城门守卫都没了。

column5: Oh yeah, I guess that {i}was{/i} your job.\nI'm glad to see that you got everything done.\nDid you happen to... touch that sword, by any chance?
column6: 哦对，我想那{i}确实{/i}是你的工作。\n很高兴看到你把事情都办妥了。\n你有没有……碰巧……碰过那把剑？

column5: Absolutely not.\nI kept it under wraps the entire time.\nWe put it in The Grand Tree for safekeeping.
column6: 绝对没有。\n我一直把它原样封存着。\n我们把它放进巨树里妥善保管了。

column5: Good idea. I'm just really curious.\nDamek was able to use it, however briefly.\nAnd not only that, but he had a vision too.
column6: 好主意。我只是非常好奇。\n达梅克居然能用它，虽然只是一瞬间。\n而且不止如此，他还看到了幻象。

column5: Yeah, I was wondering about that.\nDidn't you guys find a new spirit idol in Mazeo?
column6: 是啊，我也在想那件事。\n你们不是在马泽奥发现了一座新的灵像吗？

column5: Yeah, I think he wants to harness it for power.\nI didn't stop to ask, but it's all he talks about now.
column6: 没错，我觉得他想驾驭它来获取力量。\n我没停下来问，但这已经是他现在唯一念叨的事了。

column5: Well, isn't it inside your new HQ?
column6: 嗯，它不就在你们的新总部里吗？

column5: Yeah — now that you mention it.
column6: 是啊——你这么一说。

column5: Didn't Damek frequent those underground tunnels?\nMaybe he was exposed to some level of spiritual energy.\nAt least enough to let him have a vision, or something.
column6: 达梅克不是经常出入那些地下隧道吗？\n也许他接触到了某种程度的灵能量。\n至少足够让他看到幻象之类的。

column5: I... don't think that's how it works
column6: 我……不觉得是那么回事

column5: It's a possibility, at least give me that much.\nThat blade challenges {i}all{/i} of our understandings.
column6: 这是一种可能，至少承认这点吧。\n那把剑挑战了我们{i}所有{/i}的认知。

column5: Alright, your theory has merit.\nIt's really odd — but it makes sense.\nCan you even imagine if it was true...?
column6: 好吧，你的理论有几分道理。\n确实很古怪——但说得通。\n你能想象如果那是真的吗……？

column5: Maybe that's why Damek wants to harness its power.\nGiving regular people visions? He'd have an army of Seers.\nThere's no way The Triumvirate could fight back against {i}that{/i}.
column6: 也许这就是达梅克想驾驭它力量的原因。\n让普通人看到幻象？那他就会有一支先知大军。\n三人执政团绝不可能对抗{i}那样{/i}的力量。

column5: Whoa...\nHey, how'd you learn about this stuff anyway?
column6: 哇……\n嘿，你究竟是怎么知道这些的？

column5: I overheard a few things, that's all.\nNo one is leaking intel or anything.
column6: 我只是碰巧听到了一些事，仅此而已。\n没有人在泄露情报之类的。

column5: Good. We can't have any moles.\nThe Rebellion, as it is — currently hangs on threads.\nIt's only thanks to that anomalous blade that we stand a chance.
column6: 很好。我们不能有内奸。\n反抗军如今——正悬于一线。\n全靠那把异常的剑，我们才有机会。

column5: Hey, you were working with [firstname]?
column6: 嘿，你之前和[firstname]一起干活？

column5: Hey, you were working with [firstname]?
column6: 嘿，你之前和[firstname]一起干活？

column5: Yeah, something like that.\nIt lasted all a couple hours.
column6: 是啊，差不多吧。\n也就持续了几个小时。

column5: What do you think about him?
column6: 你觉得他怎么样？

column5: What do you think about her?
column6: 你觉得她怎么样？

column5: I honestly have no idea.\nIt's hard to believe that our fate rests upon {i}one{/i} person.\nI don't think I could put my faith in somebody that way.
column6: 我老实说不知道。\n很难相信我们的命运竟系于{i}一个{/i}人身上。\n我想我没法那样去信任一个人。

column5: Why not?
column6: 为什么不行？

column5: It's a big gamble, isn't it? Too risky.
column6: 这是一场豪赌，对吧？太冒险了。

column5: Yeah, but faith is all about risk.\nYou believe in spite of overwhelming odds.\nYou fight, even when {i}everything{/i} tells you to stop.
column6: 是啊，但信念本来就是关于冒险的。\n即使胜算渺茫，你依然相信。\n就算{i}一切{/i}都在让你停下，你依然奋战。

column5: Hmm...
You don't have to agree, but it's true.\nWithout faith, The Rebellion wouldn't even be here.\nAlestia would remain under The Triumvirate's grasp forever.
column6: 你不必同意，但这是事实。\n没有信念，反抗军根本不会存在。\n阿莱斯蒂亚将永远处于三人执政团的掌控之下。

column5: You have a point, Ulric.\nIt's impressive that you've come this far.
column6: 你说得有道理，乌尔里克。\n你们能走到这一步，真令人钦佩。

column5: And we still have a long way to go.\nBut we won't get there if people don't {i}believe{/i}.\nHave a little faith in us, alright Zamira?
column6: 我们还有很长的路要走。\n但如果人们不{i}相信{/i}，我们就到不了那里。\n对我们多一点信心，好吗，扎米拉？

column5: Well, I can't say no to that.\nJust don't let me down, alright?\nWhen we make it through this, I'm buying drinks.
column6: 嗯，这我没法拒绝。\n只是别让我失望，好吗？\n等我们熬过这一关，我请喝酒。

column5: Oh, you mean you aren't buying right {i}now{/i}?\nAnd here I was — buttering you up for nothing.
column6: 哦，你的意思是你不{i}现在{/i}请？\n我还在这儿——白拍你马屁了。

column5: Zamira, can I talk to you for a second?
column6: 扎米拉，能跟你聊两句吗？

column5: Of course. What's up, Airen?
column6: 当然。怎么了，艾琳？

column5: I want to thank [firstname] for what he's done.\nDefying Damek's orders, and letting me keep Peregrino?\nThey deserve something, but I don't know what to do.
column6: 我想感谢[firstname]所做的一切。\n违抗达梅克的命令，让我留下佩雷格里诺？\n他们该得到点什么，但我不知道该怎么做。

column5: I want to thank [firstname] for what she's done.\nDefying Damek's orders, and letting me keep Peregrino?\nThey deserve something, but I don't know what to do.
column6: 我想感谢[firstname]所做的一切。\n违抗达梅克的命令，让我留下佩雷格里诺？\n他们该得到点什么，但我不知道该怎么做。

column5: Hmm...
I was thinking of offering him a permanent room.\nYou know, to stay here whenever he wants.\nShould I offer unlimited drinks as well?
column6: 我在考虑给他提供一个长期房间。\n你懂的，他想来住就来。\n我是不是该再提供无限量饮品？

column5: I was thinking of offering her a permanent room.\nYou know, to stay here whenever she wants.\nShould I offer unlimited drinks as well?
column6: 我在考虑给她提供一个长期房间。\n你懂的，她想什么时候来住都行。\n我是不是该再提供无限量饮品？

column5: Hmm...
Zamira, are you paying attention?
column6: 扎米拉，你在听吗？

column5: Does this offer of free drinks extend to his comrades?
column6: 这免费饮品的提议也包括他的同伴吗？

column5: Does this offer of free drinks extend to her comrades?
column6: 这免费饮品的提议也包括她的同伴吗？

column5: I suppose it would.
column6: 我想会吧。

column5: Alright, I'm sold!\nHere, I'll take you to see him right away.\nI'm so thirsty — this is going to be amazing!
column6: 好，我被说服了！\n来，我这就带你去找他。\n我渴死了——这一定会棒极了！

column5: Alright, I'm sold!\nHere, I'll take you to see her right away.\nI'm so thirsty — this is going to be amazing!
column6: 好，我被说服了！\n来，我这就带你去找她。\n我渴死了——这一定会棒极了！

column5: Zamira — whoa, let go!\nI want a gift for {i}them{/i}, not {i}you{/i}!
column6: 扎米拉——哇，松手！\n我是想给{i}他们{/i}送礼物，不是{i}你{/i}！

column5: Don't worry, he'll love it!\nEverybody — Airen is giving us free drinks!\nCome over here, let's celebrate for Peregrino!
column6: 别担心，他会喜欢的！\n大伙儿——艾琳请我们喝免费酒啦！\n都过来，我们为佩雷格里诺庆祝！

column5: Don't worry, she'll love it!\nEverybody — Airen is giving us free drinks!\nCome over here, let's celebrate for Peregrino!
column6: 别担心，她会喜欢的！\n大伙儿——艾琳请我们喝免费酒啦！\n都过来，我们为佩雷格里诺庆祝！

column5: Oh no.\nIs he serious right now...?\nThere's no way I have enough for everybody.
column6: 哦不。\n他现在是认真的吗……？\n我根本不可能有足够的酒请所有人。

column5: Yeah, you heard right! Free!
column6: 对，你没听错！免费！

column5: Can you believe Damek's nerve...?
column6: 你能相信达梅克这么大胆吗……？

column5: Don't worry, he knows what he's doing.\nHe wouldn't act outside of Alestia's best interests.\nWhatever he's planning, I trust him.
column6: 别担心，他知道自己在做什么。\n他不会做违背阿莱斯蒂亚利益的事。\n不管他在谋划什么，我都信任他。

column5: Even if it means losing my tavern...?
column6: 就算这意味着失去我的酒馆……？

column5: I can't change my outlook, sorry.
column6: 抱歉，我改变不了我的看法。

column5: Alright...\nAt least you can relate to me a little.\nWithout Valinorth, your job is gone too.
column6: 好吧……\n至少你能稍微理解我一点。\n没了瓦利诺斯，你的工作也没了。

column5: Yeah, looks like we'll both be unemployed.\nMaybe we could look for a new job together.\nWe're all going to Mazeo, right?
column6: 是啊，看来我们俩都要失业了。\n也许我们可以一起找新工作。\n我们都要去马泽奥，对吧？

column5: It's the closest place to go.\nBut I think the pirates have the monopoly on that place.\nYou think the new Rebel HQ will have a tavern at all?
column6: 那是最近的地方了。\n但我觉得那里的海盗垄断了一切。\n你觉得新的反抗军总部会有酒馆吗？

column5: Beats me. But I know Mazeo has one.\nWhen we get there, how about we scout it out?\nStart looking in your comfort zone, and {i}then{/i} branch out.
column6: 我可不知道。但我知道马泽奥有一家。\n等我们到了那儿，先去看看怎么样？\n先从你熟悉的领域找起，{i}然后{/i}再向外扩展。

column5: Yeah, that's a good idea.\nThanks Zamira, you're a good guy.\nI hope you can find a new job as well.
column6: 是啊，这主意不错。\n谢谢你，扎米拉，你是个好人。\n希望你也能找到新工作。

column5: I might ask Damek if he has any openings.\nI don't need money. Just food, and a place to live.\nHe's offering that to {i}everyone{/i} from Valinorth.
column6: 我也许会问问达梅克有没有空缺职位。\n我不需要钱。只要食物和住处。\n他对{i}所有{/i}来自瓦利诺斯的人都提供这些。

column5: I guess he really {i}is{/i} a nice guy...\nBut he's taking Peregrino away from me.\nIt's hard to side with someone like that, you know?
column6: 我想他{i}确实{/i}是个好人……\n但他要把佩雷格里诺从我身边夺走。\n很难站在那样的人那边，你知道吗？

column5: I understand.\nDon't worry, everything will work out.\nWe'll need more barkeeps when this is all over.
column6: 我明白。\n别担心，一切都会好起来的。\n等这一切结束后，我们会需要更多酒保的。

column5: Really?
column6: 真的吗？

column5: Yeah, of course!\nImagine the celebrations when we win.\nThis isn't permanent. You'll be fine.
column6: 是啊，当然！\n想象一下我们胜利时的庆祝场面。\n这不是永久的。你会没事的。

column5: So, about that charm...
column6: 那么，关于那个魅力……

column5: Yeah?
column6: 嗯？

column5: When are you gonna start turning it on?
column6: 你打算什么时候把它打开？

column5: It's... been on this whole time.
column6: 它……一直开着啊。

column5: Oh boy...
column6: 哦天哪……

column5: Hey, what's that supposed to mean?
column6: 嘿，那是什么意思？

column5: It means you think highly of your own ability.\nAnd if I'm not mistaken, it's a little {i}too{/i} highly.
column6: 意思是高估了自己的能力。\n如果我没猜错的话，还{i}太{/i}高估了。

column5: That's not true!
column6: 才不是！

column5: Oh really? Charm me, then.
column6: 哦，是吗？那就来迷住我啊。

column5: You mean right now...?
column6: 你是说现在……？

column5: Yeah, right here. Right now.\nShouldn't too be hard for someone like yourself.
column6: 对，就在这儿。就现在。\n对你这样的人来说应该不难吧。

column5: Oh, well...\nJust let me think.\nIt takes a bit to \"get in the groove\".
column6: 哦，嗯……\n让我想想。\n进入状态需要点时间。

column5: Oh, is that so? Sounds like an excuse to me.
column6: 哦，是吗？在我听来像个借口。

column5: It's not!
column6: 才不是！

column5: Alright then, just hurry it up, Pro.\nI'd tell you to take your time, but I don't want to die of old age.
column6: 那好，快点吧，普洛。\n我本想让你慢慢来，但我不想老死在这儿。

column5: Hmph!
column6: 哼！

column5: Hey, Pro?
column6: 嘿，普洛？

column5: What's up?
column6: 怎么了？

column5: That can't be your real name...
column6: 那不可能是你的真名……

column5: Why not...?
column6: 为什么不能……？

column5: I mean — it's a little odd.
column6: 我是说——这有点古怪。

column5: And Valessa isn't?
column6: 那瓦莱莎就不古怪吗？

column5: Oh, you have a point...
column6: 哦，你说得有道理……

column5: But since you asked — it isn't my real name.\nThe truth is, I don't actually know my real name.
column6: 但既然你问了——它确实不是我的真名。\n事实是，我其实不知道自己的真名。

column5: How do you manage that?
column6: 你怎么会这样？

column5: I'd rather not talk about it, if it's all the same to you.\nPro is just something the orphans called me when I was younger.\nI showed a knack for picking up skills rather quickly.
column6: 如果你不介意的话，我不想谈这个。\n普洛只是我小时候孤儿们对我的称呼。\n我当时学什么都很快，显得很有天赋。

column5: So you're a pro...
column6: 所以你就是个专业高手……

column5: Something like that, heh.\nAny idea why your parents chose Valessa?
column6: 差不多吧，嘿。\n你知道你父母为什么给你取名瓦莱莎吗？

column5: No idea, actually.\nI never thought to question it.\nBut yours kinda stuck out like a sore thumb.
column6: 其实完全不知道。\n我从没想过要去质疑。\n但你的名字确实显得格格不入。

column5: I'll take that as a compliment.\nHey, there's something else on my mind, actually.
column6: 我就当是夸奖了。\n嘿，其实我还有件别的事在想。

column5: Oh yeah? What's that?
column6: 哦，是吗？什么事？

column5: What's up with the name Fortaime...?\nLike — how is that one even possible?
column6: 福泰姆这名字是怎么回事……？\n就是——这名字怎么可能存在？

column5: I've always wondered that!
column6: 我一直也想知道！

column5: It's bugging me, and I've only known him for a day.\nIt must bother you so much. You've known him forever.
column6: 我才认识他一天就被这名字困扰了。\n你认识他那么久，一定更受不了吧。

column5: Yeah! But you're good at getting info, right...?
column6: 是啊！但你不是擅长打探消息吗……？

column5: That's what I've been told.
column6: 别人是这么说的。

column5: Maybe we can work together to find this out...!\nI wanna know just what \"Fortaime\" really means.
column6: 也许我们可以合作查清楚这件事……！\n我想知道“福泰姆”到底是什么意思。

column5: Okay, let's do it!\nPro and Valessa — on the case!
column6: 好，就这么办！\n普洛和瓦莱莎——开始查案！

column5: Hey, Lillith...?
column6: 嘿，莉莉丝……？

column5: Yeah?
column6: 嗯？

column5: Is there a library in Mazeo?\nLike, a place to read up on the spirits?\nI have some stuff I'd like to look into.
column6: 马泽奥有图书馆吗？\n就是那种可以研究灵的地方？\n我有些东西想查一查。

column5: Unfortunately, no.\nThe Triumvirate seized all of that long ago.\nRumor has it that they've stuffed it all in Balteus.
column6: 很遗憾，没有。\n三人执政团很久以前就把那些全都没收了。\n有传言说他们把那些东西全塞进了巴尔泰乌斯。

column5: You mean at The Grand Library?
column6: 你是说在大图书馆里？

column5: Yeah. But I don't know for sure.\nIt's just ancient rumors at this point.
column6: 是啊。但我不确定。\n到了现在，那也只是些古老的传闻。

column5: Ancient...?
column6: 古老……？

column5: There's a group of people that say so, yeah.\nThey think life existed on Alestia before The Triumvirate.\nWhen they took over, they just stole any writing saying otherwise.
column6: 确实有一群人这么说。\n他们认为在三人执政团之前，阿莱斯蒂亚上就有生命存在。\n他们掌权后，就把所有记载相反说法的文字都抢走了。

column5: That's impossible.
column6: 那不可能。

column5: Hey, I didn't say they were a {i}smart{/i} group.\nBut nobody has been to The Grand Library to see.\nThe Triumvirate keeps such a tight grip on Balteus.
column6: 嘿，我可没说他们是个{i}聪明{/i}的群体。\n但没人去过那座大图书馆求证。\n三人执政团把巴尔泰乌斯控制得死死的。

column5: So they can't prove their theories...\nBut at the same time, we can't {i}disprove{/i} them.
column6: 所以他们无法证明自己的理论……\n但与此同时，我们也无法{i}反驳{/i}他们。

column5: Exactly.\nUnless you visit The Grand Libary.\nYou {i}are{/i} going to Balteus, right?
column6: 正是如此。\n除非你去那座大图书馆看看。\n你{i}确实{/i}要去巴尔泰乌斯，对吧？

column5: That's the end goal, yeah.
column6: 对，那是最终目标。

column5: Then maybe we'll find out soon.\nWhatever knowledge they have in there? We deserve to know.\nI'm sure Damek will open its doors to everybody after the war.
column6: 那也许我们很快就能知道了。\n不管那里藏着什么知识？我们都该有权知道。\n我相信战争结束后，达梅克会把它的大门向所有人敞开。

column5: Who do you side with, Lillith?
column6: 你支持谁，莉莉丝？

column5: What do you mean?\nLike — between Alex and Nada?
column6: 你什么意思？\n是说——亚历克斯和娜达之间？

column5: Yeah, the pirates.\nI was just curious, that's all.
column6: 对，那两个海盗。\n我只是好奇，仅此而已。

column5: Well, I don't know their demands.\nThat would play a big part in my choice.\nBut even then, it's not my place to decide.
column6: 嗯，我不知道他们的诉求。\n那会是我做选择的重要因素。\n但即便如此，也轮不到我来决定。

column5: Oh, I'm not asking you to decide.\nIt's just a hypothetical question.
column6: 哦，我不是让你决定。\n只是个假设性的问题。

column5: Hmm...
Hey, take your time!\nIt's not an easy decision, after all.
column6: 嘿，慢慢来！\n毕竟这不是个容易的决定。

column5: Alex. Hands down.
column6: 亚历克斯。毫无疑问。

column5: Or you could answer instantly...\nBut why Alex? What makes him better?
column6: 也可以立刻回答……\n但为什么是亚历克斯？他好在哪儿？

column5: He treats me with respect, that's what.\nNada on the other hand, well that's a different story.\nThe way I look at things — there's two types of people.
column6: 因为他尊重我，就是这样。\n而娜达呢，那就是另一回事了。\n依我看——人有两种。

column5: Those that use others as stepping stones for success.\nAnd those that respect others, rising to the top together.\nNada is the former, and Alex is the latter. She's ruthless.
column6: 一种是把别人当作成功垫脚石的人。\n另一种是尊重他人、和大家一起攀上顶峰的人。\n娜达属于前者，亚历克斯属于后者。她冷酷无情。

column5: She's pretty much double-crossed everybody but Gryz.\nIf that ever happens, trust me, I won't be surprised at all.
column6: 她几乎背叛过所有人，除了格瑞兹。\n如果连他也被背叛，相信我，我一点都不会惊讶。

column5: How do we know we can trust her, then?
column6: 那我们怎么知道能信任她呢？

column5: Well, her and Alex have the edge in negotiations.\nThey have what {i}we{/i} want, so they can demand anything.\nI have no doubt that Nada will try to gain power and influence.
column6: 嗯，她和亚历克斯在谈判中占上风。\n他们有{i}我们{/i}想要的东西，所以他们可以随便提条件。\n我毫不怀疑娜达会试图攫取权力和影响力。

column5: These are the things she'd usually stab others in the back for.\nBut now she has an opportunity to get it just by {i}helping{/i} Gryz.
column6: 这些正是她平时会为此背后捅刀子的东西。\n但现在她只要{i}帮助{/i}格瑞兹就有机会得到。

column5: Oh, I guess that makes sense.\nShe's only in it to get what she wants.
column6: 哦，我想这说得通。\n她掺和进来只是为了得到自己想要的东西。

column5: Yeah. And Alex on the other hand...?\nI'm sure his demands will benefit more than him.\nThat's just the type of guy he is — so I like him more.
column6: 是啊。那亚历克斯呢……？\n我敢肯定他的条件会让他以外的人受益。\n他就是那种人——所以我更喜欢他。

column5: Alright! Thanks for the information!
column6: 好！谢谢你的情报！

column5: No problem, little one.
column6: 不客气，小家伙。

column5: Hey, Gryz?
column6: 嘿，格瑞兹？

column5: Yes?
column6: 嗯？

column5: What's with that sheep around your neck?
column6: 你脖子上那只羊是怎么回事？

column5: Oh, you mean Lassiter?
column6: 哦，你说拉西特？

column5: I guess...?
column6: 算是吧……？

column5: When I was younger, I used to be a shepherd.\nBut that didn't last long before I served The Triumvirate.\nThey made me kill all my sheep before they accepted me.
column6: 我年轻时当过牧羊人。\n但没干多久，我就去为三人执政团效力了。\n他们在我被接纳之前，逼我杀光了我所有的羊。

column5: What!?
column6: 什么！？

column5: I guess it was to prove myself.\nYou know, that I'd leave my old life behind.\nI did what they said, but I kept a souvenir.
column6: 我想是为了证明我自己吧。\n你懂的，证明我会抛下过去的生活。\n我照他们说的做了，但留了一件纪念品。

column5: Oh, I see...
column6: 哦，我明白了……

column5: It's always important to remember where you came from.\nDid you bring any souvenirs from Valinorth along with you?
column6: 记住自己来自哪里总是很重要的。\n你从瓦利诺斯带了什么纪念品吗？

column5: Actually, no...\nUnless my clothes count.
column6: 其实没有……\n除非我的衣服也算。

column5: Depends who you're asking.
column6: 那得看问谁了。

column5: But you know, I'm not actually leaving Valinorth behind!\nWe'll save it, and go back one day. I know it...\nThat's one of our goals during this journey.
column6: 但你要知道，我其实并没有抛弃瓦利诺斯！\n我们会拯救它，总有一天会回去的。我知道……\n那是我们这趟旅程的目标之一。

column5: I see...
column6: 我明白了……

column5: So, Ulric...
column6: 那么，乌尔里克……

column5: Yeah?
column6: 嗯？

column5: I saw you and [firstname] in that tavern.\nYou two were getting {i}awfully{/i} close.
column6: 我看到你和[firstname]在那家酒馆里。\n你们俩靠得{i}异常{/i}近。

column5: I saw you and [firstname] in that tavern.\nYou two were getting {i}awfully{/i} close.
column6: 我看到你和[firstname]在那家酒馆里。\n你们俩靠得{i}异常{/i}近。

column5: Your point is...?
column6: 你想说什么……？

column5: You know we're kinda dating, right?\nWe had our first date in the town square.
column6: 你知道我们算是在交往吧？\n我们在城镇广场有了第一次约会。

column5: Oh, that's what that was?
column6: 哦，原来那是约会？

column5: Yeah, and it was pretty awesome!\nMostly thanks to you though, and that apple.
column6: 是啊，而且相当棒！\n不过主要还是多亏了你，还有那个苹果。

column5: I was hoping you'd share it together.\nMaybe I was playing matchmaker all along.
column6: 我本希望你们会一起分享。\n也许我一直在当媒人呢。

column5: Yeah, right! Nobody is {i}that{/i} smart.
column6: 得了吧！没人{i}那么{/i}聪明。

column5: You're not giving me enough credit, little one.\nAnyway — you don't mind that we're...?
column6: 你太低估我了，小家伙。\n总之——你不介意我们……？

column5: Oh, of course not! The more the merrier!\n[firstname] has a lot of love to go around.
column6: 哦，当然不介意！人越多越开心！\n[firstname]的爱可多得很，分得过来。

column5: Oh, of course not! The more the merrier!\n[firstname] has a lot of love to go around.
column6: 哦，当然不介意！人越多越开心！\n[firstname]的爱可多得很，分得过来。

column5: Yeah. More than I thought, actually.\nI'm sure you and I will be getting closer now, too.
column6: 是啊。其实比我预想的还多。\n我相信现在你和我也会变得更亲近。

column5: No objections here!
column6: 我这边没意见！

column5: I was just gonna say, that's pretty cool!
column6: 我正要说，那挺酷的！

column5: Really?
column6: 真的吗？

column5: He never had time for that stuff back in Valinorth, so yeah.\nIt's good to see things changing now that we're on the road.\nI didn't know this would happen. I guess I missed my chance.
column6: 他以前在瓦利诺斯时从没时间顾这些，所以嘛。\n现在上路了，很高兴看到事情有变化。\n我没想到会这样。看来我错过了机会。

column5: She never had time for that stuff back in Valinorth, so yeah.\nIt's good to see things changing now that we're on the road.\nI didn't know this would happen. I guess I missed my chance.
column6: 她以前在瓦利诺斯时从没时间顾这些，所以嘛。\n现在上路了，很高兴看到事情有变化。\n我没想到会这样。看来我错过了机会。

column5: Wait, are you jealous...?
column6: 等等，你是嫉妒吗……？

column5: No! Not at all!
column6: 不！才没有！

column5: Sure.
column6: 当然。

column5: Ulric, I'm serious!
column6: 乌尔里克，我是认真的！

column5: You know, you're still free to see him if you want to.\nOr is the culture in Valinorth different than everywhere else?
column6: 你知道的，如果你愿意，你依然可以和他交往。\n还是说瓦利诺斯的文化跟别处不一样？

column5: You know, you're still free to see her if you want to.\nOr is the culture in Valinorth different than everywhere else?
column6: 你知道的，如果你愿意，你依然可以和她交往。\n还是说瓦利诺斯的文化跟别处不一样？

column5: What do you mean..?
column6: 你什么意思……？

column5: It's normal for people to have more than one partner.\nI thought the same went for Valinorth, actually.
column6: 一个人有不止一个伴侣是很正常的。\n其实我以为瓦利诺斯也是这样。

column5: Oh, it does...!\nSorry, I must've misunderstood.
column6: 哦，确实是的……！\n抱歉，我一定是误会了。

column5: You're just dodging the issue, aren't you?\nFortaime, it's okay to admit if you like [firstname].
column6: 你只是在回避问题，对吧？\n福泰姆，如果你喜欢[firstname]，承认也没关系。

column5: You're just dodging the issue, aren't you?\nFortaime, it's okay to admit if you like [firstname].
column6: 你只是在回避问题，对吧？\n福泰姆，如果你喜欢[firstname]，承认也没关系。

column5: Never!
column6: 绝不！

column5: Hey, Fortaime?
column6: 嘿，福泰姆？

column5: Yeah?
column6: 嗯？

column5: I saw you and [firstname] run off into an alley earlier.\nWhat were you two doing back there, exactly?
column6: 我看到你和[firstname]刚才跑进了一条小巷。\n你们俩到底在后面干什么？

column5: I saw you and [firstname] run off into an alley earlier.\nWhat were you two doing back there, exactly?
column6: 我看到你和[firstname]刚才跑进了一条小巷。\n你们俩到底在后面干什么？

column5: Oh, we were on a {i}date{/i}!
column6: 哦，我们在{i}约会{/i}！

column5: What!? Seriously...?
column6: 什么！？真的假的……？

column5: Whoa, don't act so surprised — you might hurt me.
column6: 哇，别那么吃惊——你会伤到我的。

column5: No, it's not that. There's just so much going on.\nAre you sure that won't interfere with anything...?
column6: 不是，不是那个意思。只是事情太多了。\n你确定那不会影响什么吗……？

column5: Of course not! I think we're smarter than that.\nBesides, it was perfect. We shared a Mazean Apple!
column6: 当然不会！我觉得我们比那更聪明。\n再说，那太完美了。我们分享了一个马泽奥苹果！

column5: Wow, how romantic.
column6: 哇，真浪漫。

column5: You had to be there!
column6: 你得身临其境才行！

column5: I think I'll pass...\nIt's good to see you enjoying yourself, though.\nThere's just too much on my mind for that kind of stuff.
column6: 我想还是算了……\n不过看到你开心，我很高兴。\n只是我心里装的事太多，顾不上那种事。

column5: Just wait until we get to the Rebel HQ, Valessa.\nIt'll be a life of luxury, you'll see. There'll be plenty of time!
column6: 等我们到了反抗军总部你就知道了，瓦莱莎。\n那会是奢侈的生活，你会看到的。到时候时间多的是！

column5: We can dream...
column6: 做做梦还是可以的……
